title: AMD Q3 2026: record $13.4B revenue, Data Center up 97% on Instinct ramp
subtitle: AMD posted its largest quarter ever on November 3, with Data Center revenue nearly doubling year-over-year as Instinct GPU shipments accelerate into the MI350 cycle.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: AMD reported third-quarter 2026 results on November 3, with revenue of $13.4 billion — up 45% year over year and a company record. The Data Center segment grew 97% year over year, which AMD attributed to record sales of Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. Non-GAAP diluted EPS came in at $2.09, net income was $2.4 billion, and CFO Jean Hu told analysts the Q4 outlook points to accelerating growth led by continued Data Center demand.

The near-doubling of Data Center revenue matters because it is the first quarter since the MI350 series entered full production ramp. For roughly two years the AI accelerator market has been treated as Nvidia plus a long tail; a 97% growth print from AMD on a base that is no longer small weakens that framing. The segment did not break out standalone MI350 dollars, but the growth rate implies something north of $8 billion in Data Center revenue for the quarter, from a Q3 2025 base of $4.3 billion.

The result lands in a stretch of hyperscaler capex that has repeatedly been revised up — Meta at $115-$135B for 2026, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon all raising prior guides on their own Q3 calls last week. AMD's commentary suggests buyers are willing to multi-source at the top of the stack rather than concentrate spend with a single vendor, which is a meaningful shift from the posture of late 2024 and early 2025. Nvidia reports FY27 Q3 later in November and will offer the comparison point.

A takeaway for learners: an earnings release is a primary source — the 8-K and the transcript. Read the segment detail, not the headline. The headline here is 'record revenue,' which was expected. The signal is the Data Center growth rate at this quarter's base, and the fact that AMD is now a credible second supplier rather than a hopeful one. When you evaluate an AI infrastructure story, the question to carry is which part of the market structure the number actually changes.
